title: Saturation and quasi-coherence of the supported-section quotient
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $V\subseteq Y$ be an open subscheme with inclusion $j$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $H$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $K\subseteq H$ be the subsheaf defined on each open $W$ by $K(W)=\{s\in H(W):s|_{W\cap V}=0\}$, and assume that $K$ is quasi-coherent. In the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] put $Q=\operatorname{Coker}(K\hookrightarrow H)$ and let $\pi:H\to Q$ be the canonical quotient. Then $Q$ is quasi-coherent, $\pi$ is an epimorphism of sheaves, and for every open $W$ and $s\in H(W)$ one has $\pi_W(s)=0$ if and only if $s\in K(W)$. For every affine open $W$ the map $\pi_W$ is surjective. The restriction $\pi|_V:H|_V\to Q|_V$ is an isomorphism. For every open $W\subseteq Y$ and $t\in Q(W)$, the equality $t|_{W\cap V}=0$ implies $t=0$. Equivalently, $Q\to j_*(Q|_V)$ is a monomorphism: quotienting by all supported sections leaves no supported local sections. No quasi-compactness of $Y$ or $V$ is assumed beyond the stated quasi-coherence of $K$.

proof.text: Since i is mono, its factorization map to the abelian image is an isomorphism in the abelian category of module sheaves. Its components are therefore bijections. Combine this with the sectionwise range/kernel equality of step 1 to identify the kernel of the quotient projection on every open W with the actual range of i.app W. The converse follows directly from cokernel.condition.

proof.text: For W contained in V, hK and step 2 show that a section killed by the projection restricts to zero on W intersect V = W, hence is zero. Apply this to differences to obtain injectivity on every such W. Every open in V has image contained in V, so componentwise cancellation makes the restricted projection mono. The restriction functor is a left adjoint, so preserves the epimorphic quotient projection. A mono and epi in the abelian category of modules on V is an isomorphism. This replaces the explicit gluing of affine lifts by the existing adjunction and abelian-category API.

source.place: Tag 07ZP, lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, exact restriction-kernel sequence in proof of (3); quotient construction: divisors.tex Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1). proof.text: Let a quotient section t on W vanish on W intersect V. Choose for each point of W an affine neighborhood U contained in W. By step 1 lift t restricted to U to a section s of H. Naturality and the vanishing hypothesis show that the image of s restricted to U intersect V is zero. Injectivity from step 3 makes that restriction zero, so hK puts s in the image of i, and step 2 kills its quotient image. Thus t vanishes on an affine cover, and sheaf uniqueness gives t = 0. The adjunction unit is restriction to the image of the preimage of W, equal to V intersect W. Its zero kernel is therefore the vanishing assertion just proved. Apply this to differences and cancel componentwise to obtain that the unit is mono.
